ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The electric field lines of a certain electrostatic field are parallel to the x-axis, and the graph of the relationship between electric potential and the x-coordinate change is shown in the figure. It is known that the x-coordinates of points P and Q in the electric field are respectively 1m and 4m. A negatively charged particle (gravity neglected) is released from rest from the coordinate origin O. What is the relationship between the kinetic energy of the particle at point P and at point Q?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The kinetic energy of the particle at point P is equal to the kinetic energy at point Q
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: in the figure, the vertical axis is electric potential φ/V, and the horizontal axis is x/m; the φ-x graph is a broken line, and the electric potential first rises as x increases, and then decreases. Several coordinate positions are marked in the figure with dashed grid lines. Point P is located at x=1 m, and point Q is located at x=4 m; reading from the graph, both points P and Q are on the horizontal line of φ=10 V, so φ_P=φ_Q=10 V. Then reason: the particle is released from rest from the coordinate origin O, gravity is neglected, and it is acted on only by the electrostatic force, so the mechanical kinetic energy and electric potential energy satisfy energy conservation: K+qφ=constant. Although the particle is negatively charged, the electric potentials at points P and Q are the same, so qφ_P=qφ_Q, that is, the electric potential energies at the two points are the same. When the particle reaches P and Q from the same starting point O, the change in electric potential energy is the same, so the kinetic energy obtained is also the same. Conclusion: K_P=K_Q.
